clue.text: Police scan rings camouflaged to get pedestrians safely across the road

definitions.text: get pedestrians safely across the road
definitions.note: a verb phrase describing what the answer, a noun, is for

indicators.note: something camouflaged is disguised, so the letters before it appear in a disguised order

explanation.surface: Officers scanning for rings in disguise while helping people over the street.
explanation.walkthrough: A PELICAN CROSSING is a British pedestrian crossing controlled by push-button traffic lights.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of signal-controlled crossing exists precisely so walkers can traverse traffic without danger.

clue.text: County town moving fast to attract motor company

indicators.note: moving letters around puts them into a different order

explanation.surface: A town eager to lure a car maker to set up there.
explanation.walkthrough: STAFFORD is the county town (administrative centre) of Staffordshire in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Stafford serves as the administrative seat of Staffordshire, which is what a British county town is.

clue.text: Nasty points I'd included

indicators.note: something included is placed inside a larger group, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: three compass points: south, north, east
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that the remarks they slipped in were mean-spirited.
explanation.walkthrough: Points are compass points, a crossword staple for N, S, E and W.
explanation.definitionFit: A snide remark is sly and unkind, so the word is a close synonym for mean or spiteful.

clue.text: Collier, sick at heart, turns hat maker

indicators.note: being at the heart of something means sitting in its middle, so one word goes inside another

parts.note: a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: An ailing coal miner changes career to making hats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns' here means becomes, linking the wordplay to the definition rather than signalling a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A milliner designs, makes and sells hats, especially women's headwear.

clue.text: Model Philistines take in the home of the Oracle

indicators.note: the phrase says the words take something in, holding a run of letters within them

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Uncultured model citizens visit the ancient Greek oracle site.
explanation.definitionFit: Delphi in ancient Greece housed the famous oracle of Apollo, consulted by pilgrims for prophecies.

clue.text: Moral deterioration takes 10 years with the northern church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A decade of moral decline ending with a northern church.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadence is the decline in standards and self-indulgence associated with a society losing its morals.

clue.text: Eastern footballers?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as an old adjective, belonging to the East
second meaning: Leyton ..., a London football club

explanation.walkthrough: Leyton Orient is a professional football club in east London, usually just called Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means the East as a region and, poetically, eastern, and it also names a well-known English football team.

clue.text: Obscure Conservatives at Cambridge University look back and see a world of dreams

parts.note: to cloud something is to obscure it
CU for Cambridge University with C for Conservatives

indicators.note: looking back means facing the other way, so this word is read from end to start

explanation.surface: Murky student Tories look back and glimpse a dream world.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviations combine as Cambridge University Conservatives, the name of the student political society.
explanation.definitionFit: Cloud-cuckoo-land is an idiom for a fanciful, unrealistic imaginary place where impossible hopes live.

clue.text: Oriental kiss takes 10 seconds, then I've captured broad

parts.note: a kiss at the end of a letter
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An eastern kiss lasts ten seconds before someone confesses to seizing a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captured' does no work in the wordplay; it just helps the surface, which reads broad as slang for a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Extensive means covering a large area or range, so it is a synonym of wide-ranging or broad.

clue.text: Traditional knowledge about river is coming back to Mr Flynn

indicators.note: coming back means travelling the other way, so the combination is read right to left
about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: lore is knowledge passed down by tradition

explanation.surface: Old knowledge about a river returns to someone called Flynn.
explanation.definitionFit: Errol Flynn was the swashbuckling Hollywood film star, so his first name identifies the actor.

clue.text: Atheist, when at home, builds disordered life round daughter

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word letters go about the single abbreviation
disordered means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A non-believer staying home creates a chaotic life around his daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: An infidel is an unbeliever in a given religion, loosely matching someone who rejects belief in God.

clue.text: Tableland is shown in illustration by gold

parts.note: a plate is a full-page illustration in a book
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A high flat region depicted in a picture beside some gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is an elevated area of fairly level ground, which tableland names exactly.

clue.text: Years ago Gibraltar was filled with excited curiosity

parts.note: years ago means in the past; that these letters also run on into the next word is a coincidence
its initial, as in the abbreviation Gib

explanation.surface: Long ago, the Rock was buzzing with eager expectation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being agog means being eager and impatient to see or hear something, full of keen anticipation.

clue.text: Act in spite erroneously, but this will kill the germs

definitions.note: a clause describing the answer, a noun

indicators.note: doing something erroneously means getting it wrong, so the letters come out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Behaving spitefully by mistake, yet with a cleansing result.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiseptic is a substance applied to prevent infection by destroying harmful microorganisms.

clue.text: Predominate and prove confused to writer of an IOU

indicators.note: confused letters are mixed up, so they need putting into a new order

parts.note: someone who writes an IOU is one who owes

explanation.surface: Being dominant, yet muddled when called to account by a debtor.
explanation.definitionFit: To overpower is to overcome or prevail over others, close in sense to dominating them.

clue.text: Dead body is discovered by chap in vehicle

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

explanation.surface: A man sitting in his car stumbles on a corpse.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadaver is a corpse, particularly one used for medical dissection or study.

clue.text: Serene ocean

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the largest of the world's oceans

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means peaceable or tranquil, and the word also names the world's biggest body of water.

clue.text: Rustic has aspiration to capture game bird

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a rustic is a country person
the breathy sound written as H

explanation.surface: A country dweller hopes to catch a bird for the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: Aspiration is the phonetic term for an H sound, a breath before a vowel.
explanation.definitionFit: The pheasant is a long-tailed bird widely shot for sport and food.

clue.text: Wildly excited soldier pushes one past net in football club

indicators.note: in places the combined pieces inside the outer abbreviation
pushes means follows in sequence, so pieces are laid one after another

explanation.surface: An excited footballer sends the ball beyond the net at his club.
explanation.definitionFit: Frenetic means fast, energetic and uncontrolled, describing wild, frantic agitation.

clue.text: Impeded old boys caught in genuine disarray, initially

indicators.note: disarray is untidiness, so these letters are jumbled
in joins the single abbreviation to the jumbled word

explanation.surface: Former pupils find themselves in a real mess at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: 'genuine' must stand for TRUSTED, and 'initially' tells you the old boys come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstructed means blocked or hindered, so it matches impeded as a past participle.

clue.text: Seedy, but quiet, sailor who took on heartless bully

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letters are removed

explanation.surface: A shabby, timid seaman who stood up to a cruel tormentor.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby and seedy both describe something run-down, worn or disreputable in appearance.

clue.text: It'll be nearly dark in half a second going up to the trees

indicators.note: in half places one piece in the middle of the other
in a down entry, going up means reading from bottom to top
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Dusk falls in an instant as you climb up into the woods.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedars are tall evergreen conifers, so the plural answer names a group of trees.

clue.text: Support old building blocks

explanation.surface: Propping up an ancient structure of blocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is the famous plastic toy brick system that children use for building models.

clue.text: A girl meddled with holy chalice

indicators.note: meddling with something disturbs it, so the letters are moved around

explanation.surface: A young woman tampers with a sacred cup.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy Grail is the legendary cup of the Last Supper sought by Arthurian knights.

clue.text: Mixture of a dose can be made from ocean fruits

indicators.note: a mixture is a blend, so these letters are blended into a new order

explanation.surface: A medicinal concoction brewed from things harvested from the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Seafood is edible marine life, a literal rendering of the French phrase fruits de mer.

clue.text: US turning right? Genuine? Bizarre!

indicators.note: turning round sends the two letters the other way

explanation.surface: A baffled cry about American politics swinging right.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal describes something dreamlike and strange, so it shares the sense of weird or odd.

clue.text: Heroic prize giver drops the Spanish in favour of the French

indicators.note: drops says one article is let go from the word, leaving a gap to refill
choosing one thing in favour of another means swapping it in where the rejected one stood

parts.note: Alfred Nobel founded the Nobel prizes

explanation.surface: A prize founder ditches Spanish for French.
explanation.definitionFit: Noble describes having fine personal qualities such as courage and honour, close to heroic.

clue.text: Dramatic performance could tear a doctor away from ambition

indicators.note: taken away from means removed out of the following word

parts.note: A plus MB, a Bachelor of Medicine

explanation.surface: An ambitious person dreams of a stage performance tearing a medic away.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is a particular performance or interpretation of a song, role or piece of music.
